title: Stuffed Onions
subtitle: in a lemon and date syrup sauce
description: Onion layers filled with a herby tomato rice and slowly braised in a sweet and sour sauce of date syrup and lemon until caramelised.

steps.text: Make a deep cut in each onion down to the core, without separating it. Cook in a pot with water to cover over low heat for 30 to 40 minutes until the onions soften but stay whole.
Remove with a slotted spoon and let cool. Separate into individual layers (each onion gives about 7 good layers for stuffing).
Mix the filling: the raw rice, finely chopped tomato, chopped parsley, 2 tbsp olive oil, a little sugar, pepper and salt.
Fill each onion layer with a teaspoon of the rice filling, roll up and press closed.

Heat 3 to 4 tbsp olive oil in a large deep pan that fits the stuffed onions in a single layer. Pack them in tightly and fry for 5 minutes until browned, shaking the pan occasionally to turn them so they colour on all sides.

Add a little sugar, the date syrup and salt, pour in water to cover and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours over the lowest heat until tender and caramelised. Taste the sauce and balance with the lemon juice. This can be made ahead and kept in the fridge for 2 to 3 days.
To serve, reheat in the sauce, adding a little water to the pot if needed. Drizzle with a little olive oil before serving.
